say: For example, the buyer now asks Kemi for 8,000 packs by the same date. With 2% overrun, that needs about 742 packs a day. Her sustained rate is 470, so the gap is about 272 a day.

say: Option A, 2 extra fryer hours a day, gives only about 605. And 60 hours a week is above the 55-hour level that WHO and ILO link to higher risk of stroke and heart disease. Rejected.

panel.heading: 8,000 packs by the same date
items: Need 742 a day; sustained rate is 470

say: Option B, a second fryer only, makes sealing the new bottleneck. Only about 529. Far short.

panel.heading: 8,000 packs by the same date
items: Need 742 a day; sustained rate is 470

say: Option C adds a fryer, a sealer and a peeler, giving about 881. Enough, but three new people to train within days.

items: Need 742 a day; sustained rate is 470

say: Option D: Kemi keeps her proven line, and a trusted partner with a proven 300 packs a day makes the other 3,000 packs.

say: Choose a partner whose work you have seen. Visit, watch a batch, check hygiene and their output records, and put it in writing.

card.title: What a partner pack earns Kemi

say: The buyer pays 950 naira a pack. Kemi pays her partner 720 per accepted pack, and spends about 20 on inspection and transport.

card.title: What a partner pack earns Kemi

say: That leaves about 210 naira a pack, about 630,000 on 3,000 packs. Less than her own packs, but with far less risk.
Give the partner the specification sheet and a golden sample, supply the printed pouches yourself, and tell the buyer about the partner. You stay responsible for every pack.

card.title: What a partner pack earns Kemi

say: Work content means the person-minutes a station needs for 100 units. Divide it by takt time for 100 units. Kemi's takt is about 89 minutes per 100 packs.
Peeling needs 100 person-minutes, so 1.1 people, rounded up to 2.
Frying and sealing each need 1 person.
Seasoning and labelling are light, so one person does both. That is a crew of 5, with Kemi supervising.
Her two trained temporary workers take the peeling places. Experienced staff keep the fryer and sealer.

panel.heading: People per station = work / takt
panel.rule: Experienced staff hold the bottleneck and quality steps.

say: Untrained workers can create more rework than output. Kemi budgets 2 paid training days. The new worker watches a full cycle, then works beside an experienced person.
She works alone only after passing three checks in a row. Safety rules come on day one, and temporary staff do not work the fryer.

say: Exhausted workers make mistakes and get hurt. Kemi plans 48 hours a week with a full rest day, well below 55, and rotates people on repetitive tasks.

say: A missing carton is easy to settle at the door and very hard a week later. Count together, get the delivery note signed and dated, and photograph it with the stacked cartons.
Keep a few packs from each day, and send a WhatsApp the same day with the photo and a reminder of the balance due date.
Within a week, sit with your supervisor and use your records, not memory. Kemi planned 470 good packs a day. Without the power-cut day, she averaged about 448.
Why? Temporary peelers were slower in the first three days. She delivered on time because of the buffer, not because the plan was exact.
Next time she plans with about 450 a day, adds a training day, and arranges backup power.

panel.heading: Four questions within a week
panel.rule: Plan the next order with real numbers, not the old plan.

say: To remember. Size the gap and test every option on the whole line. Give partners the same specification and gates. Keep hours safe, and get a signed delivery note.
Then keep a portfolio of real evidence: your capacity statement, order summaries, photos and a buyer reference.
